record.paper_title: The Volume of Vector Fields on Riemannian Manifolds: Main Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Stability of scaled Hopf fields on Berger spheres
record.original_question: Let (S^{2m+1}, g_mu) be a Berger sphere with m > 1, let H_mu be its unit Hopf vector field, and let rH_mu be the Hopf vector field scaled to length r. Complete the classification, in the parameters m, mu, and r, of when rH_mu is stable as an r-minimal vector field for the volume functional.

evidence.quote: For .m > 1 the situation becomes quite complicated and the problem is not completely solved.
Open Problem To complete the classification of .rHμ attending its stability as an r-minimal vector field

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer m ≥ 1 and a parameter μ > 0, let S^{2m+1} ⊂ ℂ^{m+1} denote the unit sphere and let g_1 be the round metric of constant sectional curvature 1. The Hopf vector field H is the unit vector field on (S^{2m+1}, g_1) defined by H_p = i·p (regarding p ∈ S^{2m+1} ⊂ ℂ^{m+1}). The Berger metric g_μ is the canonical variation of g_1 along the Hopf fibration: it agrees with g_1 on the orthogonal complement of H and satisfies g_μ(H,H) = μ². Let H_μ = (1/μ) H, which is the unit Hopf vector field of (S^{2m+1}, g_μ). For r > 0, denote by rH_μ the Hopf vector field rescaled to have constant length r.

A smooth vector field V on a Riemannian manifold (M,g) of constant length r determines a submanifold V(M) of the tangent bundle TM (with its Sasaki metric); the volume functional vol(V) is the volume of V(M). A vector field of constant length r is called r-minimal if it is a critical point of the volume functional restricted to vector fields of constant length r, and r-stable if the second variation of the volume functional at V is nonnegative for all variations through vector fields of constant length r.

Problem. For every m > 1, determine the complete set of pairs (μ, r) ∈ (0,∞) × (0,∞) for which rH_μ is a stable r-minimal vector field for the volume functional on the Berger sphere (S^{2m+1}, g_μ).
artifact.category_tag: Minimal vector fields on Berger spheres
artifact.status_search_result: The classification is known to be incomplete for m > 1. Surveys and recent works on minimal vector fields of constant length on odd-dimensional spheres and Berger spheres treat the m = 1 case and partial results for m > 1, but state explicitly that for higher m the stability classification of rH_μ as an r-minimal vector field remains open.

status_evidence.title: Minimal Vector Fields of Constant Length on the Odd-Dimensional Spheres
status_evidence.snippet: Scaled Hopf vector fields on odd dimensional spheres are characterized as minimal (in the scaled sense), with stability determined as a function of the scale.
status_evidence.claim: Stability of rH_μ as r-minimal vector field is treated as a parameter-dependent classification problem that is not fully resolved for higher-dimensional Berger spheres.

status_evidence.title: Volume, energy and generalized energy of unit vector fields on Berger spheres
status_evidence.snippet: Stability of the volume and energy at the Hopf fields on Berger spheres depends on μ.
status_evidence.claim: Existing results on stability of unit Hopf fields on Berger spheres do not give a complete (m,μ,r) classification for m>1.
